worksheet.title: First, Next, Last
worksheet.subtitle: Putting steps in the right order
worksheet.learning_goal: I can put steps in order: first, next, last.

parts.title: Steps happen in order
parts.text: When we do something, the steps happen in order: first, next, last. Bit is building a block tower — one block, then two, then three.

parts.title: Watch Bit build — in order
parts.note: First 1 block, next 2 blocks, last 3 blocks. The tower grows in order.

parts.title: Which step is FIRST?
parts.prompt: The first step has the fewest dots. Circle the step that comes FIRST.

parts.title: Which step is LAST?
parts.prompt: The last step has the most dots. Circle the step that comes LAST.

parts.title: You try — write the order
parts.prompt: Write 1, 2, 3 under the mixed-up steps to put them in order (fewest to most).

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: Doing steps in the right order — first, next, last — is how we follow a plan. A plan made of ordered steps is called an algorithm.

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Children put the steps of an action in order — first, next, last. Ordering steps is the foundation of sequencing and algorithms: a plan is a list of steps that must happen in the right order.

parts.title: Kindergarten frame (Ontario)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children order the steps of a familiar process.
No reading required of the child: read each prompt aloud; the child circles and writes 1-2-3.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet + a pencil. Optional: real blocks to build the 1-2-3 tower in order first.

parts.title: Run it (about 15 min)
text: 1. MODEL: build the tower aloud — 'first one block, next two, last three.' The number of blocks grows.
2. GUIDED: Exercise 1 — the step with one dot comes first (fewest).
3. YOU TRY: children find the LAST step (Ex 2), then number all three in order (Ex 3).
4. Connect: 'A plan made of ordered steps is called an algorithm — computers follow algorithms.'

parts.title: Answer key (modelled by the run-gate)
text: Model — first 1 block, next 2 blocks, last 3 blocks.
Ex 1 — circle the single dot ● (fewest = first).
Ex 2 — circle the three dots ● ● ● (most = last).

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: ordering by position on the page instead of by count — have them count the dots aloud.
Simplify: order just two steps (1 then 2) before three.
Extend: add a fourth step (4 dots) and re-order, or order steps of a real routine.
Movement option: line up children shortest to tallest — that is putting things in order too.

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The child identifies the first and last steps by count and numbers the three steps 1-2-3 in order.
